entry.dc:title: Development of Coal Industry in Central Asia.
entry.dc:creator: Leleko A.
entry.dc:description: Coal deposits in Soviet Central Asia are located in the territory of three Union Republics: Uzbekistan, Kirghizia, and Tadjikistan. So far 8 coal districts have been explored, comprising 40 deposits. The total coal reserves suitable for open pit mining amount to 1. 87 billion t, including 1. 5 billion t at Angren deposit. In 1977, coal output amounted to 10. 4 Mt (including 5. 6 mt from open pit mines). output from Angren deposit is about 4. 6 Mt per annum.

entry.dc:title: SESSIONS PAPERS - AMERICAN MINING CONGRESS, MINING CONVENTION, 1977.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Proceedings contain 70 papers which are grouped into 16 sets, each of them dealing with a specific aspect of minig or mineral processing. Main subjects covered include: Use of public lands; productivity, reclamation, slurry transportation and mechanization in coal mining; impact of environmental controls on mining; minerals availability; underground and open pit mining; education of mining engineers; undersea mineral resources; safety and health in mines; mineral processing. Selected papers are indexed separately.

entry.dc:title: MINING ACTIVITY IN THE WESTERN WORLD.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: This survey covers the Western World's major producing mines classified on an ore-production basis. Data are derived primarily from a study of 22 metals and minerals. These include iron, copper, lead, zinc, tin, bauxite, gold, diamonds, platinum, manganese, nickel, uranium, chrome, mercury, molybdenum, asbestos, boron, potash, phosphate rock, tungsten, titanium and silver. Tables A, B and C in the survey mainly relate to underground and open pit mining.

entry.dc:title: MATCHING LOADERS AND TRUCKS FOR OPEN PIT MINING
entry.dc:creator: Cummings B.
entry.dc:description: For large scale surface mining operations, a variety of excavating equipment is available for different needs. Each type has its advantages. The power shovel has long life and large capacity. The rubber-tired front end loader has mobility and high cycle rates. To get the best production from any type of equipment requires the proper matching of equipment to the mining operation. The author takes a copper mine as an example.

entry.dc:title: SLOPE STABILITY INVESTIGATION AT GASPE COPPER MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Hucka V.
entry.dc:description: In view of the extensive open pit mining operation at Gaspe Copper Mines Limited, Murdochville, Quebec, Canada, a study of an optimum slope design was felt necessary. This paper describes the different steps of the slope stability project: origin and organization to achieve an optimum design. The various phases of the project were: survey of the ore body and topography, investigation of physico-mechanical properties of rocks, structural geological mapping, ground-water study, and detailed study of structural weaknesses. The results were subsequently used to analyse different modes of possible failure of rock mass. The information obtained is being used in redesigning the Copper Mountain pit. Refs.

entry.dc:title: NOVA SCOTIA PLANS BIG COAL PROGRAMS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Major developments in the Nova Scotia coal industry, including a new open pit mine in Pictou County, a series of drilling and exploration programs, and conversion of some Nova Scotia Power Corporation generating plants from oil to coal, have been announced by Premier Gerald A. Regan. The area of interest lies west of the town of Stellarton and includes seven seams of coal. A diamond drilling program carried out in co-operation with the Department of Regional Economic Expansion indicated a potential of up to 10,000,000 tons of coal accessible by open pit mining. Work will commence on engineering feasibility including detailed diamond drilling, hydrologic studies and design.

entry.dc:title: GLIMPSE AT OPEN PIT MINING IN 1976.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The article reviews developments in costs, personnel training, equipment trends and specific activities in copper, iron ore, molybdenum, phosphate, silver, gold, and uranium.

entry.dc:title: ROCK MECHANICS.
entry.dc:creator: Ross-Brown D.
entry.dc:description: Problems in open pit mining, underground design, use of numerical methods, and rock classification, are discussed. New research methods and techniques such as a pneumatic borehole packet for falling head tests in artesian conditions, are described.

entry.dc:title: AMC (AMERICAN MINING CONGRESS) MINING CONVENTION, 1976.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.prism:publicationName: AMC Am Min Congr Min Conv
entry.dc:description: Proceedings contain 61 papers dealing with various issues and problems that must be solved if the U. S. mining industry is to continue to supply America's mineral and fossil fuel demands in the quantities which will be needed in the next two decades and beyond. Key topics covered include: the importance of minerals to U. S national economy; environmental controls; use of public lands; mineral processing; coal mining; communications; exploration; finance; management; underground mining; minerals availability; undersea mineral resources; open pit mining; and safety and health in the mining industry. Selected papers are indexed separately.

entry.dc:title: Hydraulic rock drills - their role in open pit mining.
entry.dc:creator: Durk R.
entry.dc:description: The author aims at outlining the present status of the hydraulic drill in the mining industry, both surface and underground. The operating principles of both the pneumatic percussion rock drill and the hydraulic rock drill are described and compared. It is considered that the advantages of the hydraulic rock drill are (i) better performance (ii) greater efficiency (iii) reduced specific energy requirements compared with the pneumatic drills (iv) reduced fuel requirements (v) less capital cost (vi) lower maintenance costs and reduced downtime (vii) better environmental conditions - reduced noise and other pollution. Hydraulic drills manufacturwd by Dresser Industries , Ingersoll-Rand , Eimco-Secoma and Atlas-Copco are described, together with performance characteristics. Applications of such hydraulic drills include road construction, open-pit mining activities (secondary blasting operations).

entry.dc:title: BIG HOLE BLASTHOLE AT INCO.
entry.dc:creator: Green G.
entry.dc:description: For nearly two decades, Inco's Ontario Division has researched methods and equipment to improve the blasthole stoping technique. The potential of larger diameter, longer holes in underground mining has been recognized since earlier experiences with large blastholes in open pit mining. ITH (in-the-hole) drilling equipment, with 4-in. hammers, was tried unsuccessfully as early as 1962. New develop; ments in drills and button bits prompted a further investigation into the possibility of using ITH drills in underground applications. As a direct result of tests, Inco's efforts were directed toward promoting and developing drills of suitable design for caging and transporting to the drill sites without dismantling. ITH big blastholes underground are now a major source of production.

entry.dc:title: ALASKA - MINING'S CHILLY FUTURE IN THE LAND OF THE MIDNIGHT SUN.
entry.dc:creator: Carter R.A.
entry.dc:description: History and present status of operations in gold and coal mines, underwater open pit mining, and gold dredging are reviewed. Exploration of titaniferrous magnetite, copper, and nickel is described, and minerals inventory growth and marketing problems are noted. Oil well exploration is surveyed.

entry.dc:title: REGIONAL ASPECTS AFFECT PLANNING OF SURFACE MINING OPERATIONS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Conventional stripping methods are giving way to more sophisticated operational planning as mining costs and environmental regulations continue to grow. This article reviews certain specific improved mining techniques employed by the coal industry in four distinct regions of the United States. Region I was conventional contour mining methods, haulback or lateral movement operations, mountain-top removal, longwall stripping and multi-seam mining. Region II chiefly relies on box-cut contour mining, modified block-cut and block-area mining. Region III uses modified area mining, tandem-dragline operations and bucket wheel operations, while Region IV employs area mining, open pit mining and steeply dipping multi-seams.

entry.dc:title: ESTIMATE OF THE ECONOMICS OF URANIUM CONCENTRATE PRODUCTION FROM LOW GRADE SOURCES.
entry.dc:creator: Klemenic J.
entry.dc:description: Typical costs for both open pit mining and underground mining of uranium ores for 0. 01 to 0. 10 percent of U//3O//8 content are given in numerous tables. There have been significant changes in the uranium market. In 1972, under a buyer's market, prices for even the long term were seldom above 8 per pound of U//3O//8. Now, it is a seller's market. The price has been as high as 41 per pound in 1976. Because of great interest in lower grade ores, due to higher prices, a study of typical earnings was made.

entry.dc:title: OPEN PIT MINING EQUIPMENT FOR VERY HIGH RATES OF PRODUCTION.
entry.dc:creator: Krumrey A.
entry.dc:description: The development of the bucket wheel excavators and stackers of the 240,000 bank m**3/day capacity class posed many problems. These could be solved, thanks to the experience gained in the building and operation of the former 110,000 bank m**3/day capacity class. The cranes, hoists, and component handling devices were designed to facilitate all maintenance and repair work. New approaches were also adopted in evolving the conveyor drive terminals. The new principle of transfer crawlers reduces relocation work as well as investment costs. The coal will be available at moderate cost, thus helping to stabilize West Germany's energy and raw material supplies.

entry.dc:title: Environmental Impact of Open Pit Mining in the Conclusions of ″Bergbau '76″.
entry.dc:creator: Schmidt G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Gluckauf Die Fachzeitschrift Fur Rohstoff Bergbau Und Energie
entry.dc:description: Water resources protection reports from various countries and air and soil pollution control measures are discussed. A device for pyrite separation from coal shown at the Exposition is described.

entry.dc:title: COPPER OXIDE TO COPPER CATHODE: NEW CYPRUS JOHNSON OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: Argall G.
entry.dc:description: Arizona's newest copper mine - Cyprus Johnson - is pollution free from pit to cathode copper. Cyprus Johnson has a low capital investment per ton of cathode copper, 1,140 (7,200,000 capital cost for 5,000 annual tons of copper metal). By comparison, the current capital required to bring a major porphyry copper open pit mine, flotation mill, smelter, and refinery into production is from 5,500 to 6,500 per ton of copper produced. Cyprus Johnson is mining an oxide ore body, so there is no sulphur problem. Copper metal has been produced since March 1975 by open pit mining, dump for leaching, LIX64N solvent extraction, and electrowinning. Johnson is also one of the few copper operations in the world where ore is mined and placed in leaching dumps for ultimate copper recovery by LIX-electrowinning.

entry.dc:title: DESIGNING 240,000 DAILY CUBIC METER MINING SYSTEMS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: In the West German brown coal mining industry, developments have been characterized by the concentration of production in a limited number of large-scale open pit mines. This situation led to the development of bucket wheel excavators, belt conveyor systems and stackers of the 110,000 bank cubic meter per day capacity class. A new class of open pit mining equipment, capable of handling 240,000 bank cubic meters per day, is now required for the intended production increase at Fortuna, Garsdorf as well as for the handling of 320,000,000 bank cubic meters and tons per year from a depth of nearly 500 meters in the future Hambach open pit mine. These volumes correspond to a handling rate of 5. 3 cubic meters (bulk) per second. The main design and operating characteristics of the new generation of 240,000 daily cubic meter excavator and handling systems are described.

entry.dc:title: Method of Selection of an Optimal Variant of Working Particular Sectors of a Deposit.
entry.dc:creator: Yumatov B.P.
entry.dc:description: Open pit mining of nonferrous metal deposits is sometimes carried out at particular sectors. A complex method is proposed for selecting an optimal variant of working such deposits. The method is based on investigating the conditions of the mining work and plotting special graphs that establish relations between the volumes of extraction work and the output of metal, thus enabling evaluation of the efficiency of production. The method is illustrated by the example of a mining enterprise.

entry.dc:title: Growing Interest in Open Pit Mining of Brown Coal in Poland.
entry.dc:creator: Tilmann W.
entry.prism:publicationName: Gluckauf Die Fachzeitschrift Fur Rohstoff Bergbau Und Energie
entry.dc:description: In German.

entry.dc:title: OPEN PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Smith F.
entry.dc:description: Among factors influencing open pit mining in 1975 were the continuing low price of copper, inflation, the energy shortage and the legalization of gold ownership in the United States. While the traditional problems of mining still must be solved, it appears one of the most serious problems facing the free enterprise system in mining is government. Countries that have traditionally had a favorable climate are rapidly changing their attitudes. In the United States various governmental agencies are managing to withdraw huge tracts of land from mining and making restrictive laws, rules and regulations so that it is difficult and in some cases prohibitive to start new ventures.

entry.dc:title: Problem of Priority of Introduction into Service of New Iron Ore Deposits.
entry.dc:creator: Bastan P.P.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The article describes how different areas of the USSR are provided with resources of iron ore. Based on an analysis of the present-day state of affairs and of the prospect of development of ferrous metallurgy, a method of economic evaluation of iron ore deposits is given. In accordance with the proposed method, an evaluation of the deposits in the Urals, Siberia and the Far East, envisaged for open pit mining, is carried out. It is concluded that the most economic would be development of mining at the Siberian deposits: Nizhne-Angarskoye, Neryudinskoye, Ishimbinskoye, Anzasskoye, and Rudnogorskoye. In the Urals, the most economic would be the development of mining at the Shikhanskoge, Malo-Kuybasskoye, Techenskoye, and Kachkanaz deposits.

entry.dc:title: GULF MINERALS TUNING UP NEW URANIUM OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Canada's first new uranium mine in 25 years has been completed by Gulf Minerals Canada Limited, operator, in partnership with Uranerz Canada Limited. The mine and mill are located 510 miles north of Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, three miles west of Wollaston Lake. The orebody itself is located under and south of what was Rabbit Lake. That lake has now been drained to allow open pit mining of the deposit. The mill has a rated production capacity of 4. 5 million pounds of U//3O//8 annually using the acid leach solvent extraction process.

entry.dc:title: COMPARATIVE ASBESTOS MINING AND PROCESSING COSTS - ALASKA VERSUS YUKON TERRITORY.
entry.dc:creator: Bottge R.
entry.dc:description: Hard rock mining has grown in importance in the Yukon Territory during the last 10 years while Alaskan hard rock mining has declined. One asbestos deposit in Alaska is dormant, but an asbestos deposit 55 miles to the east in the Yukon Territory is being mined by the Clinton Mine Div. , Cassiar Asbestos Corp. , Ltd. In this Bureau of Mines report, the economics of mining in the two locations were derived using the Clinton mine as a model. Both deposits were assumed to be of equal size and mined by similar methods. Conventional open pit mining and processing methods were assumed, and capital and operating costs were derived using flowsheets and standard costing methods. The estimated cost for the mine, mill, and support facilities in Alaska was about 30 percent more expensive than that in the Yukon Territory. The higher labor rates in Alaska were the primary contributor to the higher construction costs; freight rates added only slightly to the total costs. Approximately two-thirds of the additional annual costs of operating in Alaska were for wages and fringe benefits. The price required for the Alaskan asbestos fiber was 356. 65 per ton compared with 287. 44 for Yukon fiber, plus or minus 20 percent. A 12 percent discounted cash flow rate of return, 100 percent equity financing, and a rapid writeoff of assets were assumed.

entry.dc:title: Maps of human perturbations in the environment (Polish)
entry.dc:creator: Leszczycki S.
entry.dc:description: Maps of pollution levels in Poland were made in 1971. The air pollution map illustrates total pollution in terms of thousands of tons of dusts and gases per year. The map on water surface pollution charts the main annual water flow in m<sup>3</sup>/sec and categorizes pollution in 4 levels of severity. The pollution of Baltic bays and coastal waters is also shown. A third map identifies areas where the earth's surface has been deformed by open pit mining or industrial waste deposits, areas of ground water disturbance, and areas in danger of radioactive contamination. The following map illustrates the destruction of vegetation, particularly forests, in 4 levels of severity. A fifth map concerns transport noise disturbances and air pollution caused by internal combustion, steam and electrical engines. On this map are shown the most important railway lines, junctions and shunting stations, the busiest highways, the most important concentrations of motor vehicles in towns, the busiest waterways, the main sea ports and airports. A sixth map refers to the erosion of soil and the use of artificial fertilizers and pesticides. A seventh map deals with refuse dumps, municipal sewage systems and industrial wastes. The eight map classifies the standard of housing in towns. A general map of human effects on the environment was constructed by superimposing the other 8 maps.
